summary: Backend+frontend E2E verification of ShahLance backend-wiring iteration. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests PASS (auth, roles, orders CRUD + scoping, review CRUD + admin hide gating, saved toggle, seller apply/decide/product, files upload, Stripe checkout URL, download gating before/after paid, forbidden for non-owner). Frontend: admin login (rajavai247@gmail.com) redirects to /dashboard/worker, JWT persisted in localStorage 'shahlance_token', session survives reload (GET /api/auth/me hydration works), /my-account redirects to /login while logged out, /api/admin/overview returns 200 for admin (users/orders/etc), buyer login OK and BuyerOrders shows all 7 tabs (all/active/completed/cancelled/saved/reviews/payments), Buy Now on /services/:id → /orders/checkout/:id → checkout-confirm-btn REDIRECTS to https://checkout.stripe.com/c/pay/cs_test_... (verified live), fresh signup client → /dashboard/buyer, fresh signup freelancer → /dashboard/worker, POST /api/seller/applications works and /seller/upload correctly shows 'Not an approved seller yet' gate before admin approval.

issues: Admin (accountType=both) is routed to /dashboard/worker on login — spec said 'routed to a dashboard' so technically OK, but a dedicated /dashboard/admin landing may be clearer for admin users.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py exposes CORS with allow_credentials=False and allow_origins from env with default '*'; combined with JWT-in-localStorage this is fine, but if you later switch to httpOnly cookies you must set explicit origins and allow_credentials=True.
Admin seed on startup (server.py L806+) correctly resets password + role if the ADMIN_PASSWORD is changed — good idempotency.
No brute-force / rate limit on /api/auth/login — password guessing is unrestricted. Consider adding a lockout after N failed attempts (per auth_testing.md guidance).
GET /api/orders returns [] for unauthenticated caller (200) rather than 401 — inconsistent with other protected endpoints. Consider requiring auth for list_orders.

PATCH /api/orders/{id}/status accepts arbitrary status strings from either buyer or seller — no enum validation and no state-machine guard (e.g., a buyer could set status='completed'). Consider role-scoped transitions.

PUT /api/auth/me accepts an arbitrary dict and $sets it directly (except id/email/passwordHash/role) — a user can inject arbitrary fields like 'isSeller':true. Recommend Pydantic model for the patch body.
Password policy is not enforced server-side (min length / complexity) — client validation only.
server.py is ~840 lines and holds all routes + storage + auth helpers — approaching the 700-line split threshold; consider splitting into routers/*.py.
